slides: Welcome. In this lesson we learn two things about dividing whole numbers. First, divisibility signs, quick clues that tell us whether a number divides by another number, without calculating. Then remainders, the part that confuses many students. We only need small, simple divisors, exactly what the exam asks about.

slides.say: When we say a number is divisible by two, we mean it divides by two with nothing left over. For example, five hundred thirty-eight divided by two. Half of five hundred is two hundred fifty. Half of thirty-eight is nineteen. Together that's two hundred sixty-nine, a whole number. So five hundred thirty-eight is divisible by two.
at: five hundred thirty-eight divided by two

slides.say: Let's start with the signs most of us already know. A number is divisible by two when it's even, and that's decided by its last digit. Five hundred thirty-eight ends in eight, which is even, so it's divisible by two. Seven hundred forty-one ends in one, which is odd, so it's not.
at: A number is divisible by two
Five hundred thirty-eight ends in eight

slides.say: A number is divisible by five when its last digit is zero or five. Four hundred sixty ends in zero, and three thousand eight hundred fifteen ends in five, so both are divisible by five. Two hundred fifty-three ends in three, so it's not.
at: A number is divisible by five
Four hundred sixty ends in zero
Two hundred fifty-three ends in three

slides.say: And a number is divisible by ten when its last digit is zero, like nine hundred forty. Nine hundred forty-five ends in five, so it divides by five, but not by ten.

Now the new ones. A number is divisible by three when the sum of its digits is divisible by three. Take nine hundred forty-two. Nine plus four is thirteen, and thirteen plus two is fifteen. Fifteen is divisible by three, so the whole number, nine hundred forty-two, is divisible by three.
at: A number is divisible by three when

slides.say: Another one, five hundred twenty-three. Five plus two plus three is ten. Ten is not divisible by three, so five hundred twenty-three is not divisible by three either.

Nine works exactly the same way. If the digit sum is divisible by nine, the number is divisible by nine. Eight hundred forty-six. Eight plus four is twelve, and twelve plus six is eighteen. Eighteen is divisible by nine, so eight hundred forty-six is too. But nine hundred forty-two has a digit sum of fifteen, which doesn't divide by nine. So it divides by three, but not by nine.
at: Nine works exactly the same way
has a digit sum of fifteen

slides.say: Four and eight are a little harder. For four, we look only at the number made by the last two digits. Two thousand seven hundred sixteen ends in sixteen, and sixteen is divisible by four, so the whole number is divisible by four.

Why only the last two digits? Split the number into two thousand seven hundred, plus sixteen. A hundred is twenty-five fours, so every whole hundred is divisible by four, and so is two thousand seven hundred. That leaves only the last two digits to check.

A second example, five hundred thirty-four. The last two digits are thirty-four. Thirty-two is eight fours, and thirty-four is two more, so thirty-four is not divisible by four, and neither is five hundred thirty-four.
at: The last two digits are thirty-four

slides.say: For eight, we do the same thing with the last three digits, because a thousand is a hundred twenty-five eights. So every whole thousand is divisible by eight. In seven thousand two hundred forty, we check two hundred forty. Two hundred forty is thirty eights, so seven thousand two hundred forty is divisible by eight. Now change it by one, to seven thousand two hundred forty-one. Then we check two hundred forty-one. That's thirty eights plus one, so it's not divisible by eight.
at: For eight, we do the same thing
a thousand is a hundred twenty-five eights
Two hundred forty is thirty eights

Then we check two hundred forty-one
so it's not divisible by eight

slides.say: By the way, division by eight is very rare on the exam. And when it comes, the numbers are friendly ones from the times table, like a hundred sixty, three hundred twenty or five hundred sixty. [pause] I'll see you in the next part.
at: division by eight is very rare
